lessons.title: upstream #53272 removed native HunYuan implementations — transformers-backend HunYuanVL e2e fails in 3 escalating rounds (placeholder format → torch_npu non-contiguous → multimodal RoPE channels 4 vs 3)
lessons.symptom: run 32645452079 (8/23, job 97209485805): step-1 covered d53b1c2e "Remove native Hunyuan V1 and VL implementations (#53272)"; test_multimodal_vl[hunyuan-vl] failed all 3 e2e rounds, run ended 0/13 steps completed → manual review issue #14785, no PR. Round escalation: (r0) ValueError: HunYuanVL image placeholders must be formatted as <｜hy_place▁holder▁no▁100｜><｜hy_place▁holder▁no▁102｜><｜hy_place▁holder▁no▁101｜> ... (HunYuanVLProcessor.validate_inputs, model vllm-ascend/HunyuanOCR); (r1) RuntimeError: Only c10::MemoryFormat::Contiguous is supported for creating a npu tensor (vision encoder GELU); (r2) ValueError: Expected 4 multimodal RoPE channels, got position_ids with shape (3, 1, 8192) (transformers modeling_hunyuan_vl.py:823, HunYuanVLVisionPatchEmbedding.forward).
lessons.root_cause: d53b1c2e deleted vllm's built-in hunyuan_v1.py/hunyuan_vision models — HunYuan-VL now runs through the transformers backend, which has stricter input contracts than the native path. The adapter's first-attempt fix deleted patch_hunyuan.py and added: (1) patch_hunyuan_vl.py wrapping MultiModalDummyInputsBuilder.get_dummy_text to wrap the bare image_token as <image_start><image_token><image_end> (passes validate_inputs); (2) patch_transformers_conv.py monkey-patching Conv2dLayer/Conv3dLayer._forward_mulmat to return .contiguous() (vLLM's matmul conv path returns view().permute() non-contiguous; CUDA tolerates it, torch_npu elementwise ops reject it). r0 and r1 were genuinely fixed by these two patches — r2 is a NEW unsolved contract: transformers HunYuanVL derives multimodal RoPE axis count from len(config.text_config.rope_parameters.mrope_section) == 4 for this model, but the position_ids the vllm side produced had only 3 channels (3, 1, 8192). 3 e2e fix rounds exhausted → revert → 0 steps completed → issue #14785. Note: the same d53b1c2e adaptation was already attempted in PR #14778 (8/22 run, also failed at later steps, still open/unmerged), so main's verified.commit stayed at 27ec8ac and the 8/23 run had to re-do the hunyuan step from scratch.
fix_guidance: Placeholder contract: HunYuanVLProcessor.validate_inputs rejects a bare image_token in dummy text — dummy inputs must carry the full <image_start><image_token><image_end> triple (or go through the processor chat template). Wrapping get_dummy_text is the right hook; keep the type() processor check so other models are untouched.

torch_npu contiguous contract: ANY transformers-backend vision tower routed through vLLM's matmul conv path (_forward_mulmat returns view().permute()) will hit 'Only c10::MemoryFormat::Contiguous is supported for creating a npu tensor' on elementwise ops (GELU). .contiguous() on the mulmat output is a safe generic fix (no-op when already contiguous; CUDA unaffected).

Multimodal RoPE channels: position_ids channel count MUST equal len(rope_parameters.mrope_section) of the model config (4 here: position/width/height/image_index axes per get_rope_index). The failing shape (3,1,8192) means the vllm-side position_ids builder emitted one axis too few — check how the transformers-integration/multimodal position_ids are constructed for this model and either make the builder read mrope_section, or patch the HunYuanVL model path on the ascend side to emit 4 axes. Do NOT add a token-type axis blindly: get_rope_index also consumes mm_token_type_ids.

Version pinning: transformers hunyuan_vl modeling is a recent module (its RoPE/placeholder validation changed across versions) — record the exact transformers version in the step before attributing the failure to the adapter.

Context: the d53b1c2e adaptation already exists in open PR #14778 (partially adapted, unmerged); vllm-ascend main's verified.commit was advanced to ba07e4a4 by PR #14746 (merged 8/24). Prefer reconciling against those diffs over re-adapting hunyuan from scratch when the step range overlaps.
